ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 creating the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 12 February 2019; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended through 2023) regarding the SCSp; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the corporate charter and certificate of incorporation of each direct corporate partner or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official Commercial/Trade Register in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961) or, for non-Hague jurisdictions, Luxembourg consular legalization; plus certified French or German translation if the source language is not an accepted RCS language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card copy of each natural-person beneficial owner and of the authorised signatory of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National authority of residence or apostilled notarial copy issued by a notary in the jurisdiction of such person
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarised identification verified before a Luxembourg notary or a regulated AML professional; if executed abroad, the notarial certificate must carry a Hague Apostille or be legalised in the relevant consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (recent extract) for the corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry in the corporate partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Luxembourg consular legalization; accompanied by an official translation into French or German

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales, LSC), Articles 100-1 to 100-15 (SCSp chapter introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013); complemented by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Luxembourg City, Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg; online e-file portal: www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution (limited partnership agreement) together with the fiche électronique (electronic disclosure sheet), filed electronically via the LBR eFile platform and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The SCSp has no statutory minimum paid-up capital, no share-capital notion and no escrow account requirement under Articles 100-1 to 100-15 LSC; initial partnership interests are freely fixed in the limited partnership agreement and may be subscribed in cash or in kind, with the contributions stated in the fiche électronique for information only.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE GENERAL PARTNER OF [•] SCSp — Adopted this [date]. FIRST: the limited partnership agreement (contrat de société) is approved and the subscription of partnership interests by the initial partners is accepted. SECOND: the registered office is established at [address], Luxembourg, and the domiciliation arrangement with [registered office agent] is ratified. THIRD: [name] is appointed manager (gérant) of the general partner and is authorised, acting individually, to file the constitution deed and fiche électronique with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), to submit beneficial-owner filings to the RBE, to appoint the VAT (TVA) representative where required, to open banking accounts, and to issue LME warrant and documentary-credit instructions. FOURTH: all prior, incidental actions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Partner KYC/AML clearance and drafting of the limited partnership agreement (LPA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary or licensed corporate services provider; AML framework: amended Law of 12 November 2004 on anti-money laundering.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect certified passport copies, proof of residence and source-of-funds statements for each general and limited partner; verify ultimate beneficial owners; draft the LPA containing the legal form, registered office, corporate purpose (wholesale arbitrage of refined copper cathodes, ISIC 4662 / NAICS 423510), capital contributions and governance of the general partner; authenticate each partner's identity before signature.
required_dossiers: Certified passport or ID of each partner
Draft LPA and fiche électronique data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AML/KYC pack is incomplete, the notary or law firm issues a deficiency list; documents are resubmitted within 10 business days; signatures must be notarized before any RCS submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the constitution deed (acte de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notarial deed) or the partners by private writing in accordance with Article 100-4 LSC.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the LPA before the notary or sign a private deed with original signatures of all partners; ensure the registered office consent (lease or domiciliation agreement) is physically signed; confirm the appointment of the manager of the general partner and any restricted authority of the limited partners.
required_dossiers: List of partners and capital subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If execution is queried for legal invalidity, a rectificative deed (acte rectificatif) is executed before the same notary at the responsible partner's cost; no RCS filing is attempted until rectification is complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic inscription in the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — RCS, via the LBR eFile platform (www.lbr.lu).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed LPA, the fiche électronique and the registered office consent through the eFile portal; pay the EUR 70 inscription fee; after validation, obtain the RCS registration number and certificate; the statutory excerpt is transmitted for RESA publication.
required_dossiers: Acte de constitution (LPA) in printable format
Identification of the general partner and manager
Power of attorney for the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, the filing agent corrects the fiche électronique within 15 days; if the deed is rejected for legal defects, a notarial rectificative act is filed within one month; erroneous registration entries may be corrected by a requête en rectification submitted to the RCS judge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Legilux — Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS acceptance, the statutory notice (date of constitution, legal form, registered office, identity of the general partner, RCS number) is published automatically in the RESA; third-party effectiveness runs from publication; retain the publication confirmation for banking and counterparty KYC.
required_dossiers: No separate dossiers — publication is automatic from RCS registration data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA excerpt contains a factual error, request a correction through the RCS eFile portal within one month; where the error is attributable to the registrar, a rectified extract is republished without additional state fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of beneficial owners with the RBE register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), via LBR eFile or MyGuichet.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS inscription, submit the natural-person beneficial owners (including the controlling partners of the SCSp) with full names, nationalities, dates of birth, residential addresses and nature and percentage of interest; use the RCS registration number as reference.
required_dossiers: UBO details of each beneficial owner
Ownership or control percentages and nature of interest
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE queries the data, file an amendment promptly; late or incomplete RBE filings expose the SCSp to administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and publication of the penalty under the Law of 13 January 2019.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT (TVA) registration for intra-EU copper cathode trading
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — VAT (TVA) administration, via MyGuichet / Guichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Luxembourg VAT registration form together with the RCS certificate and manager identification; describe the intended supplies and acquisitions of copper cathodes, potential use of VAT suspension in customs warehouses, reverse-charge transactions and expected turnover; await issuance of the TVA number.
required_dossiers: Identity of the manager and partners
Description of trading flows and warehouse addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT requests clarifications, respond via MyGuichet within 15 days; where the TVA number is pending, the AEDT may issue an attestation de dépôt to facilitate customs clearance and documentary-credit negotiation; an objection to an AEDT decision may be lodged within one month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie — Direction de l'industrie (no industrial licence applies to ISIC 4662); for environmental aspects: Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et du Développement durable — Administration de l'environnement.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — wholesale physical arbitrage of refined copper cathodes (ISIC 4662 / NAICS 423510) does not require a separate operating or manufacturing permit under Luxembourg law; a class-4 établissement classé declaration may apply only if closed metal storage is established in Luxembourg under the Law of 9 May 2014 on classified establishments.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA screening required: wholesale trading of refined copper cathodes is not listed in Annexes I or II of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; no environmental report or impact study is required for an office-based trading SCSp. A class-4 declaration could apply to any future on-site warehouse holding copper cathode bundles.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC or emission thresholds apply to pure trading operations. If warehousing is conducted, compliance with the Law of 9 May 2014 (classified establishments), the Law of 21 March 2012 (waste management) and the amended Law of 19 December 2008 (water management) is required; copper cathodes are non-hazardous and no waste-handling permit is expected, but storage areas must prevent contaminated stormwater runoff and municipal sewer discharge limits must be observed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for office-only registered premises. If the SCSp later operates a copper cathode warehouse in Luxembourg, the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) must approve fire-safety features, the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) is competent for workplace safety clearance, and storage racks require a structural-load verification under the Labor Code (Book IV) and the Law of 9 May 2014 on classified establishments.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg VAT and registration duties: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), with e-portal www.aedt.public.lu and MyGuichet.lu for company and VAT filings. Direct income taxes: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), www.impotsdirects.public.lu. The business registry (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated under the Ministry of Justice, issues the corporate matricule and is accessible via www.lbr.lu and the MyGuichet.lu e-filing portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SCSp: (1) execute and file the partnership deed (contrat de société) with the RCS via a registered professional (avocat or fiduciary) on MyGuichet.lu to obtain the company matricule and the national registration number; (2) request VAT registration on AEDT Form 640 (national form; Form 640E for EU-established taxable persons; Form 640 for non-established persons, with appointment of an AEDT-approved tax representative where required); (3) receive the Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits, shown on the RCS excerpt and the AEDT registration certificate; (4) obtain an EU EORI number (Luxembourg prefix LU) for customs exports; (5) file the local 'newly established taxable person' notification if non-resident partners have no Luxembourg permanent establishment; expected completion time is 2–6 weeks from complete filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent for Luxembourg income tax: it has no legal personality and is not subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax at entity level. Profits are allocated directly to partners: a Luxembourg-resident general partner is taxed on its share; non-resident limited partners are taxable only if the SCSp creates a Luxembourg permanent establishment (e.g., through Luxembourg management or decision-making) or derives Luxembourg-source fixed assets. For VAT only, the SCSp is treated as an independent taxable person and must register separately. Territorial_Scope: non-resident partners with no Luxembourg PE are outside direct tax nexus; Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable; Entity_Level_Taxation: not applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply a US-style check-the-box election; the SCSp is transparent as a matter of legal form (law of 10 August 1915). Available mechanisms: (i) advance tax agreement or rescrit procedure with the ACD (Circular L.G. - A n°29) to confirm fiscal transparency, absence of PE, and allocation of profits; (ii) contractual election in the partnership agreement to determine partner profit shares, with mandatory proposal of substance documentation; (iii) the mandatory EU/ATAD anti-hybrid rules (law of 21 December 2018) will recharacterize effects where a double deduction or deduction-without-inclusion arises from differing classifications in Luxembourg and the partner jurisdiction; (iv) an option under the VAT Law to apply the intra-Community acquisition rule or the reverse-charge mechanism for certain cross-border B2B supplies, but no entity-classification VAT election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 as amended, implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a Luxembourg-established small business, the VAT registration threshold is EUR 35,000 annual turnover (excl. VAT) per the SME franchise regime of Article 57 of the VAT Law; businesses exceeding EUR 35,000 must register and charge VAT. A wholesale copper-cathode trading entity (ISIC 4662) will almost always exceed EUR 35,000 in turnover and is therefore required to hold a Luxembourg VAT identification number from the first taxable supply of goods, with no further threshold for non-established foreign suppliers (threshold EUR 0 in the absence of a Luxembourg fixed establishment); intra-EU distance-sales thresholds (EUR 10,000) do not apply to B2B wholesale metal trading.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently maintain a real-time fiscal clearance system, digital stamping device, or API-based invoice-clearance mandate for domestic B2B transactions. Since 1 January 2020, electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2G contracts through PEPPOL-BIS 3.0. B2B e-invoicing is permitted but not yet compulsory; the Ministry of Finance has announced the phased introduction of mandatory B2B e-invoicing, with draft legislation proposing PEPPOL-compliant e-invoices for Luxembourg VAT payers from 1 January 2026 (status: ongoing legislative process; deferral to 2027 under public discussion). For exports, the single electronic customs declaration (SAD/EX) must be lodged in the EU's Import-Control-System/Export-System (ICS2/AES), providing the CS/MRN registration number; no national stamping or pre-clearance of invoices is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of non-ferrous copper cathodes to destinations outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT under Article 42(1) of the Luxembourg VAT Law, provided: (a) the goods are physically dispatched or transported from Luxembourg to a non-EU country; (b) the goods leave the EU within 90 days from the date of supply; and (c) proof of export (electronic export declaration and transport documents) is held within the same 90-day period. Offshore services directly connected with the export (e.g., freight, handling, insurance, pre-carriage) may also be zero-rated under Article 44(2); intra-EU B2B supplies to a customer holding a valid EU VAT number are taxable at 0% under Article 43 with proper VIES validation and an Intrastat goods-movement declaration. The taxpayer must evidence the sale, movement, and consideration with contemporaneous documents.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice referencing LME Grade A copper cathodes and HS code 7403.11 (incoterms, quantity, unit price, warrant serial number)
Electronic customs export declaration (SAD/EX-A) with MRN issued in the EU Export Control System (AES)
Bill of Lading (ocean) or CMR/air waybill evidencing departure from the EU within 90 days of supply
Packing list and independent weight certificate
LME warrant or registered warehouse receipt transferring title to the non-EU buyer
Bank documentary evidence: SWIFT MT700/MT103, documentary letter of credit, or remittance advice
Inward remittance certificate or FX repatriation record (settlement within 180 days delivery baseline)
EORI number and VIES confirmation of the intra-EU customer (for 0% intra-EU supply)
Intrastat declaration for intra-Community trade movements if applicable
Evidence of delivery terms and transport insurance policy
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT targets export zero-rating in commodity trading audits. If the exporter fails to produce the export declaration, transport proof, or evidence of payment within the statutory 90-day exit period, the supply is recharacterized as a domestic taxable supply at 17% VAT, with retrospective reassessment. The general VAT assessments limitation period is 5 years from the end of the relevant calendar year, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud. Under-assessment penalties: late-payment interest at the statutory quarterly rate (approx. 3.75% p.a. in 2024), a 10% late-payment surcharge, and administrative fines up to EUR 15,000 for non-intentional documentation infringements. Intentional export fraud is criminally sanctioned with fines up to EUR 25,000 or imprisonment, and the export zero-rating is denied retroactively. The taxpayer must retain the full export and payment dossier for 6 years, and the general anti-abuse doctrine (abus de droit) applies to transactions lacking economic substance or genuine commercial rationale, permitting the clawback of zero-rating benefits and the imposition of penalties in accordance with Article 10(1) and Article 11 of the VAT Law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential supervision and AML/CFT oversight are exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance holds policy competence for financial regulation and capital-movement legislation. Luxembourg has no dedicated foreign-exchange administration agency; exchange-control functions are discharged through EU treaty law, BCL statistical reporting, and CSSF enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility applies under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. The euro is the domestic currency; USD, CNY, GBP and all other freely traded currencies are convertible without BCL approval, prior licence, or repatriation obligation. Profit remittance by an SCSp faces no FX regulatory hurdle; distributions are governed by the partnership agreement and tax treatment at the partner level. Practical friction points are limited to EU/UN sanctions screening, AML source-of-funds verification, Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA)/Common Reporting Standard (CRS) reporting, and BCL balance-of-payments statistical declarations for transactions exceeding reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio for export proceeds. A copper-cathode trading SCSp may retain USD or other foreign currency balances in multicurrency accounts, settle via SWIFT, and convert at commercially negotiated rates. All transfers of funds must comply with Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers; physical cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more require declaration under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (blocked, attestable for investor evidence) and Multicurrency Operational Account (EUR/USD/GBP)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BGL BNP Paribas S.A., Luxembourg Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with dedicated Trade Finance (Documentary LC) sub-limits and Commodity Finance desk
Operational Account with Commodity Export Pre-financing and LME-related treasury lines
Institutional USD clearing account, custody of LME warrants, and overnight FX/liquidity sweep

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury rails; acceptable only for ancillary operating expenses and small-value disbursements. Legal constraints: a non-EEA offshore digital EMI cannot provide payment accounts to a Luxembourg SCSp without a Luxembourg or EU/EEA authorisation under the Law of 20 May 2011 on payment services and e-money (PSD2 passporting); such authorisation requires substantial substance, a local compliance function, and CSSF prudential capital. A CSSF-licensed EMI can execute SEPA Credit Transfers and MT103-style payments through partner banks, but cannot issue or confirm documentary letters of credit, cannot hold LME warrants, and generally triggers higher correspondent fees, reduced settlement certainty, and enhanced compliance scrutiny for commodity-trading flows exceeding USD 1 million per transaction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible for EU/EEA-domiciled directors and UBOs using CSSF Circular 12/552-compliant video identification (e.g., regulated eIDAS/IDnow-type solution). However, Luxembourg Tier-1 banks apply a de facto requirement for at least one in-person interview at the Luxembourg branch when the SCSp: (i) has non-resident individual UBOs, (ii) operates in the higher-risk commodity wholesale segment, or (iii) shows significant cross-border volume. A physical office in Luxembourg is not a statutory condition, but a local registered address, a Luxembourg-resident general partner (or an authorised AIFM where applicable), and demonstrable local substance are effectively mandatory for opening a full commercial banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp transparency gap: the entity lacks separate legal personality (unless optional personality is elected), and the UBO chain may extend through multiple non-EU partnerships or holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement; certificate of registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); current extract from the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) under the Law of 13 January 2019; UBO declaration forms with passport copies; organisational chart showing direct and indirect ownership percentages; professional CVs and bank references for each 25%+ UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo exposure: copper cathodes may originate from, transit through, or be traded with counterparties in jurisdictions subject to EU restrictive measures, including non-EU high-risk third countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-transaction trade file: LME-approved warehouse warrant, commercial invoice, full set of bills of lading, analysis certificate, contract of sale with Incoterms 2020; counterparty sanctions screening results against EU, UN, OFAC, and UK consolidated lists; country-of-origin certificates; corporate sanctions-compliance policy; senior-management sign-off on all jurisdiction risk assessments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero minimum capital and pass-through status can trigger a shell-entity or speculative-trading red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg substance memorandum; copy of registered office agreement and local administration contract; payroll and social-security filings if any staff are employed; board and general partner meeting minutes demonstrating local decision-making; projected cash-flow model and confirmed trading pipeline with named LME member brokers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injections from non-EU sister companies without a documented source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investor source-of-funds dossier: audited financial statements, solvency certificates, bank reference letters from the remitting bank, underlying contribution resolution, SWIFT confirmation referencing the partnership agreement, and a use-of-proceeds business plan explaining the arbitrage model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commission payments to brokers or intermediaries that appear disproportionate or insufficiently identified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed broker mandate or intermediary agreement; commission schedule benchmarked to market practice (generally 0.1% to 0.5% of notional); full KYC package of the broker; evidence of independent compliance escalation and approval by the SCSp's designated AML responsible officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Split payments, rapid round-tripping, or same-day equaling in and out transfers inconsistent with a physical trading cycle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy manual; FX risk management policy; month-end trade reconciliation register; LME Clear and broker confirmations; documentary evidence that all payments map to an underlying warrant transfer, LC, or freight instrument; unconditional audit trail access for the bank's compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route: the remitting bank initiates a SWIFT MT103 to the Luxembourg account bank, referencing the beneficiary as '[Name] SCSp' with its IBAN and specifying the remittance information field as 'Capital contribution in accordance with partnership agreement dated [date]; injection into LU__LU__LU_SCSP'. Luxembourg requires no specific FX purpose code; the receiving bank will request the SCSp's LEI, RBE extract, contribution resolution, and a completed CRS/FATCA self-certification. Non-EUR inbound funds are converted at the receiving bank's spot rate on T+2; there is no BCL approval or prior notification, but the BCL may collect the transaction in its statistical balance-of-payments survey. The bank will reject transfers from non-EU crypto exchanges, pooled third-party wallets, or opaque corporate vehicles lacking a documented economic rationale.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct settlement of LME warrant transfers and spot cargo purchases; (ii) irrevocable documentary letters of credit (UCP 600 / eUCP 2.0) issued or confirmed by the Luxembourg relationship bank, payable against seller's presentation of commercial invoice, bill of lading, analysis certificate, and LME warrant delivery; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated EU counterparties; (iv) for exchange-traded LME contracts, settlement via LME Clear requires the SCSp to maintain cash margin with a clearing member broker, funded through MT103 transfers to the broker's segregated client account; (v) MT202 for interbank cover payments when the SCSp instructs a non-bank counter-transfer. All outbound MT103s must include the underlying invoice number and trade reference to satisfy Article 5 of Regulation (EU) 2015/847; payments to sanctioned jurisdictions or dual-use risk routes are blocked by automated compliance filtering.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX outright forwards (plain vanilla, T+N maturities) under ISDA 2002 and the FX Global Code; exempt from mandatory EMIR clearing.
FX swaps (simultaneous spot purchase and forward sale, or vice versa) for rolling liquidity management across USD/EUR.
EUR/USD cross-currency swaps for long-dated funding and margin optimisation, documented under ISDA/CSA with collateral posting.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) and non-deliverable swaps (NDS) limited to restricted or inconvertible currencies such as offshore CNY, INR or BRL; uneconomical for USD/EUR where full deliverability exists.

Plain vanilla OTC currency options (EUR call / USD put and covered positions) permitted under a written treasury policy; subject to EMIR transaction reporting to an authorised trade repository using the SCSp's LEI.

Exchange-traded LME Grade A copper futures and options used to hedge the physical arbitrage margin, cleared through LME Clear via a member broker; permitted as a price-risk hedge under the SCSp's trading mandate.
Money-market deposits and spot T+2 FX conversions for short-term liquidity allocation; no structured or exotic derivatives are permissible without express general partner approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registry maintenance fee (Redevance annuelle RCS) for continued active registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Invoices are issued annually; payment falls due by 30 June following the invoice date or the date stated on the RCS invoice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment triggers reminder fees and may lead to suspension of RCS extracts, denial of clean-standing certificates, and, after repeated defaults, administrative strike-off (radiation) of the registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) deposit, where statutory accounts are prepared under Lux GAAP
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end (extensions are possible only by reasoned court order)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is signalled by the RCS to the Public Prosecutor; the court may impose an administrative penalty (amende) and, after repeated non-compliance, the entity may be struck off compulsorily.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership (RBE) register declaration – event-driven filing of ultimate beneficial owners; no annual duplicate declaration when data is unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after any change in the beneficial ownership of the SCSp; initial registration at creation; no separate annual confirmation certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 per violation under the Law of 13 January 2019; persistent false or missing declarations may be prosecuted before the Luxembourg criminal courts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit becomes compulsory when the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three size thresholds at the balance-sheet date: total assets EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average number of full-time employees 50. Above these thresholds the SCSp is treated as a large undertaking and a Luxembourg-approved statutory auditor (réviseur d’entreprises) must be appointed and the audit report filed with the RCS together with annual accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual accounts are prepared under Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and annual accounts; IFRS is permitted for voluntary application and mandatory for Luxembourg entities with listed securities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing. The SCSp must maintain an accurate RBE entry at Luxembourg Business Registers and file any change within one month. The registered agent should perform an annual compliance reconciliation between the RBE record and the register of limited partners; if no change has occurred, no electronic declaration is due for that year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners and transfers of partnership interests
Register of Managers and management powers
